title: Conjugate tensor comparison identifies localization counits on all complexes
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small relative to its module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category, lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Here a functorial flat resolution means a functor to flat objects equipped with a natural epimorphism to the identity, and $M,N$ below range over $D(\mathcal A)$. Let $E:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal M$ be an additive exact equivalence with fixed quasi-inverse $H$, unit and counit satisfying the triangle identities, and a specified strong symmetric monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Assume $E,H$ preserve flat objects (tensor with the object is exact), acyclic complexes (all cohomology objects vanish), and K-flat complexes, meaning that tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Use unbounded integer cochain complexes, homotopy localizations $q_{\mathcal A},q_R$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], signed direct-sum total tensors [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], the specified termwise total comparison $t_{P,Q}:E\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(EP\otimes EQ)$, and localization factors $\kappa_P:D(E)q_{\mathcal A}P\cong q_REP$.
Fix the internal K-flat derived tensor $B_{\mathcal A}$ and the independently constructed ringed-site tensor $B_R$ [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Write $\varepsilon^{\mathcal A}_{P,Q}:B_{\mathcal A}(q_{\mathcal A}P,q_{\mathcal A}Q)\to q_{\mathcal A}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ and $\varepsilon^R$ for their canonical derived-to-ordinary localization transformations on every complex pair. Their inverses on flat-term K-flat pairs are denoted $r^{\mathcal A},r^R$. Conjugate $B_{\mathcal A}$ by $D(E),D(H)$ to a section bifunctor $B_c$, with its fixed comparison $\theta_0:D(E)B_{\mathcal A}(M,N)\cong B_c(D(E)M,D(E)N)$ obtained from the equivalence unit. Define its localization transformation $\varepsilon^c$ by the following equation on all termwise $E$-images, then by the equivalence counit on arbitrary complex pairs:
$$\varepsilon^c_{EP,EQ}\,B_c(\kappa_P,\kappa_Q)\,\theta_{0;q_{\mathcal A}P,q_{\mathcal A}Q}=q_R(t_{P,Q})\,\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}\,D(E)(\varepsilon^{\mathcal A}_{P,Q}).$$
There is a unique natural isomorphism $\theta:D(E)B_{\mathcal A}(M,N)\cong B_R(D(E)M,D(E)N)$ whose value on flat-term K-flat $P,Q$ is
$$\theta_{q_{\mathcal A}P,q_{\mathcal A}Q}=B_R(\kappa_P,\kappa_Q)^{-1}\,r^R_{EP,EQ}\,q_R(t_{P,Q})\,\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}\,D(E)(r^{\mathcal A}_{P,Q})^{-1}.$$
The natural isomorphism $v:B_c\cong B_R$ specified by $v_{D(E)M,D(E)N}\theta_{0;M,N}=\theta_{M,N}$ satisfies
$$\varepsilon^R_{U,V}\,v_{q_RU,q_RV}=\varepsilon^c_{U,V}$$
for every pair of complexes $U,V$, without any K-flatness or flat-term hypothesis on them. In particular this identifies the localization transformations, not only the derived bifunctors. All statements permit independent object and morphism universes of the site. Composition in these formulas is read right to left.

proof.text: Identify two-sided total-tensor K-flatness with categorical K-flatness by the definitions. Apply the native derived tensor universal property on the K-flat first factor, then transport the invertible Qh tensorator through the homotopy quotient factorization to obtain invertibility of internalCounit. Every other arrow of imageCounit is an isomorphism. For a site resolving pair U,V, use inverse preservation of K-flatness to apply this to HU,HV; the explicit counit extension formula then shows that conjugateCounit is invertible at U,V.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; explicit equivalence-unit/counit and naturality-square calculation, using the published cochain rigidity and site counit APIs

proof.text: Restrict conjugateCounit and the fixed site counit to the full category of flat-term K-flat cochain pairs. The latter equals the inverse fixed model map by counit_existsUnique. Their ratio is a natural isomorphism. Full faithfulness of cochain representative restriction lifts this ratio to a unique isomorphism v from conjugateTensor to the fixed independent site tensor. Lift the isomorphism with FullyFaithful.preimageIso, so inverse identities hold without choosing functorial resolutions.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; explicit equivalence-unit/counit and naturality-square calculation, using the published cochain rigidity and site counit APIs

proof.text: The transformation v inverse followed by conjugateCounit is another site localization transformation. On resolving pairs cancellation of the lifted ratio makes it exactly the inverse model map. Uniqueness in counit_existsUnique therefore identifies this transformation with the fixed counit on all complex pairs. Multiplication by v proves the required all-complex equation; no arbitrary-complex counit or ordinary tensor of resolution maps is inverted.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; explicit equivalence-unit/counit and naturality-square calculation, using the published cochain rigidity and site counit APIs

proof.text: Prove directly that counit extension along an equivalence restricts back to its given transformation, using naturality along the equivalence unit and the triangle identities; extending an already restricted transformation returns it. Hence comparisonOnSection of theta-zero followed by v is v, and theta-zero followed by comparisonOnSection of any theta is theta. A general naturality-square cancellation lemma rewrites Normalized exactly as the counit equation on termwise E-images of resolving pairs, using the localization factors and the fixed model map.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; explicit equivalence-unit/counit and naturality-square calculation, using the published cochain rigidity and site counit APIs

proof.text: For any normalized theta prime, the preceding square gives its counit equation on E-images of resolving complexes in A. For a resolving site pair U,V apply it to HU,HV, which have flat terms and are K-flat by the hypotheses. Naturality along the termwise equivalence counit EHU to U, EHV to V transfers the equation to U,V; only the derived bifunctor of this isomorphism is canceled. Full faithfulness of cochain representative restriction and cancellation of the invertible site model map imply comparisonOnSection theta prime equals v. Its image equation then implies theta prime equals theta. This proves existence, uniqueness, the specified image equation, and the all-complex counit equation.

lean.statement: theorem conjugate_tensor_localization_counit (hflat : ∀ X : A, ObjectProperty.flat X → IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (e.functor.obj X)) (hflatInv : ∀ X : Modules R, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) X → ObjectProperty.flat (e.inverse.obj X)) (hacyclic : ∀ P : CochainComplex A ℤ, P.Acyclic → ((e.functor.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).Acyclic) (hacyclicInv : ∀ P : Complexes R, P.Acyclic → ((e.inverse.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).Acyclic) (hkflat : ∀ P : CochainComplex A ℤ, P.IsKFlatForTotalTensor → CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients ((e.functor.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) (hkflatInv : ∀ P : Complexes R, P.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients → CochainComplex.IsKFlatForTotalTensor ((e.inverse.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) : (∃! θ : tensor (DerivedCategory A) ⋙ e.functor.mapDerivedCategory ≅ e.functor.mapDerivedCategory.prod e.functor.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients J R, Normalized R e θ hflat hkflat) ∧ (∀ θ : tensor (DerivedCategory A) ⋙ e.functor.mapDerivedCategory ≅ e.functor.mapDerivedCategory.prod e.functor.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients J R, Normalized R e θ hflat hkflat → (∀ M N : DerivedCategory A, (comparison e.mapDerivedCategory (tensor (DerivedCategory A))).hom.app (M, N) ≫ (comparisonOnSection R e θ).hom.app (e.functor.mapDerivedCategory.obj M, e.functor.mapDerivedCategory.obj N) = θ.hom.app (M, N)) ∧ (∀ U V : Complexes R, (comparisonOnSection R e θ).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj U, DerivedCategory.Q.obj V) ≫ (counit R).app (U, V) = (conjugateCounit R e).app (U, V)))
